dish: Ayam penyet — smashed fried chicken with sambal
address: Kim San Leng Coffee Shop, Blk 511 Bishan Street 13, S570511
w: The Bishan outlet of the well-loved Uncle Penyet chain, tucked into the same Kim San Leng coffeeshop as Ming Kee — a hearty halal plate of crispy-yet-juicy smashed fried chicken over rice with deep-fried tau kwa, greens and a punchy belacan sambal.

address: KPT Coffeeshop, Blk 284 Bishan Street 22, S570284
w: A hawker-priced Indian stall that draws steady queues to KPT coffeeshop — its prata dough is kneaded well and cooked thinner and crispier than most, and the $6 chicken biryani comes loaded with a huge, fall-apart curry chicken leg; a shorter-queue alternative to the famous Serangoon North branch.

dish: Malaysian-style dry wanton mee with char siew
address: Shunfu Mart Food Centre, Blk 320 Shunfu Road, S570320
w: A Shunfu Mart corner stall with no English sign but a constant queue — Malaysian-style dark-sauce wanton mee from $3.50, its springy noodles cooled in cold water before a return to hot, crowned with thick slices of tender char siew; named among Daniel Food Diary's best wanton mee in Singapore.

dish: Handmade mee hoon kueh by Gen Z hawkers
w: A mee hoon kueh stall run by three 20-year-old friends above Bishan Bus Interchange, hand-tearing dough to order — soupy or dry ban mian, you mian and ee mian with al-dente noodle pieces, minced pork, ikan bilis and a sweet dark sauce; a young-hawker story covered across the food press.

address: Jin Fa (Gim Huat) Kopitiam, 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024
w: Old-school charcoal-grilled kaya toast in the same Sin Ming kopitiam as Sin Ming Roti Prata — thick, fluffy white loaves toasted over charcoal for a characteristic char, layered with kaya and butter at about $1.20; a Sin Ming breakfast institution.

dish: Teochew braised duck rice & salted-vegetable duck soup
address: Blk 22 Sin Ming Road, Sin Ming Ville, S570022
w: A Sin Ming braised-duck stall with lunchtime queues among the oldest HDB blocks in the estate — tender Teochew-braised duck with a nice layer of fat under a light-but-savoury dark herbal sauce, best paired with the salted-vegetable duck soup, from about $4.50.

The Sin Ming branch of the famed Two Chefs zi char, in a three-storey building in the estate — its signature butter pork ribs are fried crisp and tender then dusted with a slow-cooked butter-milk powder that eats like cereal prawns; other stars include cereal prawn, drunken cockles and coffee pork ribs.

A long-running, wallet-friendly Bishan Thai zi char built for group sharing — its Tom Yum Seafood ($16) arrives bubbling in a claypot overflowing with fresh seafood, and the fried fish comes crisp outside, moist within; most meals land under $10 a head.

dish: Thai fried kway teow (pad thai with gravy) & deep-fried fish
address: The Canteen @ Midview City, 18 Sin Ming Lane, S573960
w: A Thai-inspired zi char in the Midview City industrial canteen where chef Mr Ang's signature is a Thai-style fried kway teow served pad-thai-meets-gravy the way his Sin Ming regulars prefer — alongside a thin, crisp deep-fried fish with chilli dip, all at hidden-gem prices.

dish: Wok-hei egg fried rice with house sambal
address: New Century Food House, Blk 151 Bishan Street 11, S570151
w: A hidden Bishan Street 11 stall doing four styles of egg fried rice with five toppings and a wok-hei lift — the savoury, spicy house sambal studded with crispy dried shrimp is what elevates it; portions run generous with a juicy chicken or pork chop.

address: Bishan Public Library, 5 Bishan Place, Level 1, S579841
w: The Bishan-library outpost of Kings Cart Coffee Factory (of the Joo Chiat roastery) — a peaceful, naturally-lit spot inside the tree-house library for micro-roasted specialty coffee in flavours like matcha, coconut and pandan, plus tea cakes and souffle.

A hidden indie roastery-cafe on the Sembawang Hills / Upper Thomson edge of Bishan, warmed by wood furnishings — micro-roasted coffee and subtle takes on brunch staples like the Thus Breakfast (sous-vide eggs, hollandaise, apple-cider sausage, back bacon).

dish: Handcrafted cakes in reusable glass jars
w: A cosy 20-seat dessert cafe beside Bishan MRT from self-taught baker Jody Ang, known for trifle-like cakes layered in reusable glass jars — strawberry-custard, lychee-passionfruit and more — plus meringue waffles whipped from an egg-white-and-soy-milk batter.

dish: All-day brunch in a Bishan Park glasshouse
address: 1382 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Bishan Park II, S569931
w: A pet-friendly garden bistro nestled in the greenery of Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park II, its roof planted over with foliage — an all-day casual menu of eggs benedict, buttermilk pancakes and a signature crab aglio olio, a longtime brunch destination in the park.

A beloved artisanal gelateria across from Bishan Interchange whose Pear, Ginger & Ginger Flower won 'Singapore's Best Gelato' at the Singapore Gelato Championship, its pistachio stone-ground for 10 hours. The Bishan outlet is now permanently closed (the brand continues in Hougang and Bedok); kept here, flagged.

dish: Blue pea flower mee hoon kueh, MSG-free broth
w: A Sin Ming coffeeshop stall where owner Joy hand-tears colourful mee hoon kueh coloured with real blue pea flowers she grows herself — super-QQ noodles in a robust, MSG-free pork-bone broth with a made-from-scratch chilli dip; a Sin Ming food-trail hidden gem.
